source: AI-assisted content generation (ChatGPT), practical synthesis checklist derived from FAO Cambodia and ACSEP marketing documentation — pending farmer/RUA verification
text: Before selling, a Preah Vihear smallholder should work through a practical checklist: (1) identify exactly what is being sold — quantity, quality/grade, condition; (2) check the realistic buyer options for that specific commodity (collector, trader, market, mill, processor, cooperative, direct consumer); (3) compare net price, not the quoted price — subtract transport, packaging, grading, fees, storage, and expected losses; (4) confirm how the product will be measured (kilograms, sacks, per animal, live weight) and use a scale where possible; (5) ask what specifically causes quality deductions before negotiating; (6) confirm payment timing before delivering; (7) weigh transport cost carefully before choosing a distant buyer over a nearby one; (8) check whether storage is actually feasible (suitable space, drying, protection from moisture/pests) before deciding to wait for a better price — most products, especially fresh vegetables, milk, and mangoes, do not tolerate long storage; (9) adjust expectations for the wet season (roughly May–October: muddy roads, drying difficulty, transport delays) and dry season (roughly November–April: heat, dust, water constraints); (10) identify the actual crop variety or animal type rather than assuming a named Cambodian variety/breed applies; (11) check whether combining volume with neighboring farmers (aggregation) is worthwhile for reaching a larger buyer; and (12) record the completed sale (date, product, quantity, buyer, quoted price, deductions, transport cost, final amount received, payment date) so future comparisons rely on actual transactions rather than memory. No specific Preah Vihear price, buyer, or variety should be assumed — this checklist should surface the farmer's actual situation, not fill it in for them.
